scenario: AITA for not helping a woman at walmart | I (male 24) started working at walmart for the summer about a month ago. My job mainly involves working with inventory in the back room and not on the floor with customers, sometimes we get heavy boxes that we need to lift as a part of our regular duties. One of my co-workers is a female (fcw) in her early to mid 30s, physically in good shape and as far as I can tell no physical disabilities. (Fcw) approaches me and asks if I can help her lift a heavy box, I say of course and I walk over to the box with her expecting us to perform a team lift - however we get to the box and as I get to one side of the box expecting her to go to the other she just stands there and watches me. I ask "are you ready?" And she says "yes it just needs to go in that bin" (referencing a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I say "ok let's do it" and she responds "it's to heavy for me can you please lift it into the bin?". I respond by saying "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me" and (fcw) said "if you're not willing to help me I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later on the head guy on our team (not my boss just the guy with most seniority who directs us) walks up to me and said " I just spoke to (fcw), the next time someone asks for help you need to help them, that's part of being a team. I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying "we're both paid to do the exact same job and if she cant perform the tasks then she shouldn't have taken the job, I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team and if you would like to discuss this further we can do it with HR present", and at this point feeling pretty annoyed, it was my turn to storm off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? Because so far it seems like its 2 against 1.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I was the asshole in this situation. Let me start by going through what happened step by step. First, I'm a male, 24 years old, working at Walmart for the summer. My job is mainly in the backroom dealing with inventory, which includes lifting heavy boxes as part of regular duties. One of my coworkers is a female in her early to mid-30s, physically in good shape, and as far as I can tell, she doesn't have any physical disabilities. One day, this female coworker approached me and asked if I could help her lift a heavy box. I agreed and walked over to the box with her, expecting us to do a team lift. But when we got to the box, she just stood there watching me. I asked, "Are you ready?" and she said, "Yes, it just needs to go in that bin" (referring to a metal shelving unit about 4 feet high). I said, "Okay, let's do it," and she responded, "It's too heavy for me. Can you please lift it into the bin?" I replied, "I'm more than happy to help anyone if they're having trouble with something, but I'm not going to lift all your heavy boxes for you while you stand there watching me." She then said, "If you're not willing to help me, I'll find someone who will" and stormed off. Later, the head guy on our team (not my boss, just the guy with the most seniority who directs us) walked up to me and said, "I just spoke to [FCW], and the next time someone asks for help, you need to help them. That's part of being a team." I responded by clarifying exactly what happened in case she stretched the truth and finished by saying, "We're both paid to do the exact same job, and if she can't perform the tasks, then she shouldn't have taken the job. I'm not the designated heavy lifter on our team, and if you would like to discuss this further, we can do it with HR present." At this point, I felt pretty annoyed and stormed off. So, was I the asshole in this situation? It seems like it's 2 against 1, with the head guy and the female coworker against me. First, I need to consider the context. We're both paid to do the same job, which includes lifting heavy boxes. The female coworker is physically in good shape, so it's reasonable to assume she can perform the task. However, she asked for help, which is a valid request in a team setting. When I agreed to help, I expected a team lift, but she didn't move to help. Instead, she asked me to do it all alone. That's where the issue arises. I felt that I was being asked to do her job for her, which isn't fair. I made it clear that I'm happy to help if she's having trouble, but I'm not here to do all her heavy lifting. The head guy then told me that I need to help when someone asks, as part of being a team. I explained my side, emphasizing that we're both responsible for the same tasks and that I shouldn't be the one doing all the heavy lifting. I also mentioned that if she can't perform the tasks, she shouldn't have taken the job. Now, considering whether I was the asshole, I need to evaluate both my actions and the expectations in the workplace. On one hand, teamwork is crucial, and helping a teammate is part of being a good team member. On the other hand, there's a line between helping and doing someone else's job for them. If she can perform the task, it's reasonable to expect her to do so, especially since we're both paid for the same responsibilities. I also need to consider the potential implications of setting a precedent. If I always do her heavy lifting, she might continue to rely on me, and it could lead to resentment or an imbalance in the team dynamics. Additionally, the head guy's instruction to help when asked could be interpreted as a directive to support teamwork, but it's also important to communicate clearly about expectations and boundaries. In this situation, I think I handled it appropriately by setting boundaries without being disrespectful. I made it clear that I'm willing to help if she's struggling, but I'm not here to do her job for her. However, storming off after the conversation might have come across as unprofessional, even if I was annoyed. Overall, while I understand the importance of teamwork, I also believe in fairness and equal responsibility. In this case, I don't think I was the asshole, but there could have been a more diplomatic way to communicate my boundaries without storming off.
